aboutH2: Envision Mind Care: psychiatry, TMS and addiction care in Edmonton
intro: Envision Mind Care is a private clinic in downtown Edmonton, at 9807 106 Street NW near the Alberta Legislature. It is mainly an outpatient practice, with psychiatrists, psychologists, family doctors, a TMS service and physiotherapy under one roof, treating depression, anxiety, OCD, ADHD, trauma, chronic pain and addiction.

For substance use, there are two routes. You can do the outpatient program on weekdays and go home each night, or stay in a private bedroom at the clinic for a six-week in-patient program, which can be extended. Envision is on the Government of Alberta's list of licensed residential addiction treatment service providers. The approach is non-12-step and trauma-informed.

pillars.title: Outpatient days or a six-week stay
pillars.body: Both versions of the substance use program start the same way, with assessments by addiction specialists, psychologists and psychiatrists that look at your use, your health, any trauma and conditions like depression, anxiety or ADHD. Outpatients come in Monday to Friday, between 8:15 am and 5 pm, and keep living at home in Edmonton, St. Albert or Sherwood Park. In-patients stay in a private bedroom at the clinic for six weeks, longer if the team recommends it, and get the same psychiatry, TMS, counselling, workshops and yoga plus dietitian sessions. The clinic keeps groups small.

pillars.title: TMS and medication alongside counselling
pillars.body: Envision puts a lot of weight on what it calls brain health. TMS sessions can be added to target cravings, withdrawal and low mood, using MagVenture and BrainsWay machines, and the clinic has given about 15,000 sessions to more than 300 people. A psychiatrist reviews your medication throughout, and medication-assisted treatment is used for opioid, alcohol or other dependence when it fits. Counselling uses CBT, DBT and motivational interviewing. Psychedelic-assisted treatment exists at the clinic but only for specific cases where standard care has failed.

pillars.title: Follow-up from the same team
pillars.body: When you finish, you leave with a written aftercare plan. That includes continued access to therapy, follow-ups with the addiction counsellors and psychiatrists you already know, and help getting back into work and daily life. Because the clinic also runs a full psychology service, people often keep seeing a psychologist there for trauma, anxiety or relationships after the addiction program ends. Families can get help understanding addiction-related behaviour and improving communication at home.

overview: The clinic describes itself as one of Western Canada's largest private mental health clinics. Its people include Medical Director and consultant psychiatrist Dr. Karthikeyan Ganapathy, a second consultant psychiatrist, registered psychologists, two GPs, a TMS therapist, a physiotherapist and a massage and osteopathic therapist. Psychology on its own covers ADHD assessment, OCD, PTSD and complex trauma, grief, burnout and addictions, using EMDR, CBT, ACT, exposure and response prevention, Hakomi and narrative therapy.

Envision has programs for particular groups: veterans, first responders, teachers, executives and professionals, and Indigenous communities. It also works with Alberta employers, including oil sands companies, on programs for their staff. It runs workshops too, such as a six-week online ADHD psychoeducation group.

faqIntro: Answers come from Envision Mind Care's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Envision Mind Care an inpatient or outpatient rehab?
faqs.a: Both, though most of what the clinic does is outpatient. Its substance use disorder program has an outpatient version, Monday to Friday while you live at home, and a six-week in-patient version where you stay in a private bedroom at the clinic. Envision is listed by the Government of Alberta as a licensed residential addiction treatment service provider.

faqs.q: How long is the in-patient program?
faqs.a: The clinic says the in-patient substance use program is six weeks, with the option to stay longer based on clinical assessment. Its program summary describes four to six weeks plus follow-up sessions. The outpatient substance use program runs about three to six weeks, also with follow-up.

faqs.q: Where does the in-patient program take place?
faqs.a: At the main clinic. Envision says both its in-patient and outpatient programs run at 9807 106 Street NW in downtown Edmonton, near the Legislature Building, and in-patient clients sleep in private bedrooms on site. Free parking is available next to the building.

faqs.q: What does a day in the outpatient program look like?
faqs.a: The outpatient program runs five days a week, with sessions between 8:15 am and 5:00 pm and the odd appointment outside those hours, including Saturdays. It covers psychiatry visits, TMS, weekly one-to-one addiction counselling, substance use education workshops, psychology group sessions and yoga. The clinic keeps groups small.

faqs.q: What is TMS and how is it used for addiction?
faqs.a: Transcranial magnetic stimulation uses magnetic pulses through a coil on the scalp to stimulate parts of the brain. Health Canada has approved it for depression that has not responded to other treatment. Envision adds TMS sessions to some substance use plans, saying it may help reduce cravings and withdrawal and lift mood alongside counselling.

faqs.q: Does Envision Mind Care offer ketamine or psychedelic therapy?
faqs.a: The clinic's site mentions ketamine therapy and has a page on psychedelic-assisted treatments. It says these are not first-line care and are only considered after a full medical and psychiatric assessment, when standard treatment has not worked, and under physician supervision. Envision says it holds an Alberta psychedelic drug treatment services licence and CPSA accreditation for psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy.

faqs.q: How much does treatment cost, and does insurance cover it?
faqs.a: Envision does not publish program prices, so call for a quote. Substance use treatment is mainly private pay, with payment plans, and the clinic notes that most insurance plans do not cover private addiction treatment. Veterans, teachers and first responders on disability may be able to use their benefits, and psychology sessions can be direct billed to several insurers.

No. Envision accepts self-referrals by phone at 780-306-2345 or through the self-referral form on its contact page. Doctors can also refer patients with the physician referral form. The clinic notes a wait of 14 weeks or more for ADHD referrals.

faqs.q: Does Envision Mind Care offer detox?
faqs.a: The clinic does not describe a stand-alone medical detox unit, and its recovery.com profile lists detox as not offered. Medication-assisted treatment can be used within the program to help with withdrawal symptoms and cravings. If you are drinking heavily or using opioids daily, ask the intake team whether you need withdrawal management first.

The team page lists Medical Director and consultant psychiatrist Dr. Karthikeyan Ganapathy, consultant psychiatrist Dr. Robert Mallet, registered psychologists Dr. Hansen Zhou and Sarah Riediger, two general practitioners, a TMS therapist and a manual osteopathic and massage therapist. Physiotherapist Hemalatha Nagarathinam is registered with the College of Physiotherapists of Alberta.

faqs.q: Can people from outside Edmonton or Alberta attend?
faqs.a: Yes. The clinic says out-of-province clients can use its programs and that people come from across Canada and abroad. The in-patient option suits people from places like Fort McMurray, Grande Prairie or Red Deer who cannot travel into Edmonton every day.
